native_route_summary.cap_caveat: The 256 lifecycle receipts were exhausted before the failed TeX wheel. No conclusion may be drawn from absent later Focused/CursorLeft/Destroyed logs. Wheels have an independent cap of512, with only2 used, so absence of a third native MouseWheel is meaningful.

proven_boundary: Both Typst wheels reached the native boundary with matching incoming/current E3B7 WindowId and produced fresh raw sequences1 and2, then table offsets changed.
The configured TeX wheel was posted with foreground PID344, but no third native MouseWheel was logged and no fresh raw sequence/time appeared during the timeout; the TeX grid offset remained0.

The trace does not establish whether the failed wheel reached NSApplication, which NSWindow/NSView AppKit selected, or whether it was discarded before Winit callback. It therefore isolates failure upstream of the observed native window-event boundary, not a precise OS/AppKit cause.
All3 configured events share flags536870912, scroll/momentum phases0, timestamp0, source_state1, and window metadata0. Those fields do not distinguish the failure.

Successful native arrivals occurred after the driver subprocess had already returned/reaped (~17/22ms estimated). A requirement that the posting process remain alive is contradicted by these controls; immediate exit is not a demonstrated cause.
source_analysis: Driver posts globally to cghidEventTap; its foreground PID guard does not target a native window. posted stdout and exit0 acknowledge emission only. CGEventPost returns void, and SDK documentation describes stream insertion before taps, not delivery acknowledgment.
Winit NSApplication sendEvent override special-cases only Command KeyUp and forwards scroll events to the original implementation.

Winit NSView scrollWheel calls mouse_motion then unconditionally queues MouseWheel. mouse_motion outside-bounds return is confined to that helper and cannot itself suppress subsequent scroll-wheel queueing. Phase0 maps to Moved.

Winit maybe_queue_event dispatches immediately or queues a run-loop closure on reentrancy. No focus/viewport wheel filter is present before the observed eframe entry. Live subsequent inspection frames exclude a globally stopped event loop, but no instrumentation proves whether this particular wheel reached that queue.
reliable_test_contract: Separate configured input emission from fresh native delivery and fresh egui consumption. A table-scroll result is interpretable only after a new native receipt tied to the current window incarnation and a new raw sequence/time for this post.

A single globally posted event with no delivery acknowledgment must remain an unavailable/failed input check, not evidence that a TextEdit consumed or blocked scrolling. No automatic retry or alternate event route was added.
limits: No GUI input, app launch, Cargo, source edit, or product fix was performed for this review.
